g1|variants|edi order to invoice.family_title: EDI Order to Invoice (OTC B2B Integration)
g1|variants|edi order to invoice.summary: This family covers the end-to-end B2B document exchange for customer orders, order confirmations, advance shipping notices, and billing via EDI. Variants differ by inbound/outbound flow, standard format (EDIFACT vs ANSI X12), and IDoc basic types processed within SAP S/4HANA OTC.

variants.name: Inbound Customer Purchase Order (ORDERS / 850)
variants.when_used: Customer transmits electronic purchase orders directly from their ERP into SAP S/4HANA to automatically create sales orders.
variants.key_config: Partner profiles (WE20), inbound process code ORDR, customer master EDI partner functions, and output control determination.

variants.name: Outbound Order Confirmation (ORDRSP / 855)
variants.when_used: SAP automatically acknowledges the receipt and processing of the customer purchase order, communicating confirmed quantities and dates.
variants.key_config: Output type BA00 / EDI, partner function SP, message determination, and condition records (VV31 / NACE).

variants.name: Outbound Advance Shipping Notice (DESADV / 856)
variants.when_used: Outbound delivery is posted with goods issue, triggering an electronic notification to the customer detailing shipment contents and packing structure.
variants.key_config: Output type LD00, delivery-related output determination, packing hierarchy (HU management), and partner profiles.

variants.name: Outbound Customer Invoice (INVOIC / 810)
variants.when_used: Billing document is released to accounting, generating an electronic invoice transmitted to the customer for payment settlement.
variants.key_config: Output type RD00 / EDI, billing output determination, partner profile setup for invoicing party, and tax classification.

variants.name: Inbound Order Change Request (ORDCHG / 860)
variants.when_used: Customer modifies an existing open sales order electronically, updating quantities, requested delivery dates, or materials.
variants.key_config: Inbound process code ORDC, change rules in sales document type, and partner profile configuration for change message.

variants.name: Inbound Order Status Inquiry (ORDRSP / 869)
variants.when_used: Customer queries the real-time fulfillment status of an open order via automated B2B messaging.
variants.key_config: Inbound function module assignment, status report configuration, and partner profile mapping.

g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound cus.title: Inbound Customer Purchase Order via EDI (ORDERS05 / X12 850)
g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound cus.story: Computers cannot talk to each other without a translator, so companies send purchase orders as coded electronic letters that SAP turns into a real sales order automatically. Technically, this process ingests an incoming ANSI X12 850 or EDIFACT ORDERS message via Application Link Enabling (ALE) and Intermediate Documents (IDocs), mapping partner profiles, ports, and message control parameters to execute inbound function module IDOC_INPUT_ORDERS, creating standard sales document type OR.
g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound cus.why_business_needs_it: Processing thousands of customer orders manually via phone or email causes typos, slow fulfillment, and high labor costs. Automating inbound purchase orders through EDI eliminates manual keying errors, reduces order processing time from hours to seconds, and accelerates the entire Order-to-Cash cycle.

modules.role: Receives the inbound IDoc, validates customer and material master data, maps segments to sales order fields, and creates the primary sales order document.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for credit checks and billing, and MM/LE (Materials Management / Logistics Execution) for delivery creation and inventory assignment.

g1|core|edi order to invoice|outbound or.title: Outbound Order Confirmation (ORDRSP / 855) via IDoc
g1|core|edi order to invoice|outbound or.story: Just like telling your friend you got their letter and are packing the toys, the system sends an electronic acknowledgment back to the customer when their purchase order is accepted. Technically, the Sales Order output determination triggers IDoc generation using basic type ORDRSP05 via message control, transmitting confirmation data externally.
g1|core|edi order to invoice|outbound or.why_business_needs_it: It provides the customer with formal electronic confirmation of their purchase order details, pricing, and quantities. This ensures supply chain alignment and prevents fulfillment discrepancies before delivery.

g1|core|edi order to invoice|outbound ad.story: Imagine a smart delivery truck that automatically sends a digital packing list to the customer the exact moment it leaves the warehouse. g1|core|edi order to invoice|outbound cu.story:
Computers send electronic bills directly to our customers so they get paid faster without paper.

g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound ord.title: Inbound Order Change Request (ORDCHG / 860) processing to Sales Order update
g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound ord.story: Just like a customer writing an email to change their mind about an order before it ships, this process lets an external system send an electronic message to update an existing SAP sales order. Technically, it uses an inbound Intermediate Document (IDoc) with message type ORDCHG and basic type ORDERS05 to trigger function module IDOC_INPUT_ORDCHG, updating sales order fields via function module SD_SALES_DOCUMENT_CHANGE.
g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound ord.why_business_needs_it: Automating purchase order changes saves customer service teams from manual data entry while ensuring order fulfillment precisely matches the customer's latest requirements. It maintains high Order-to-Cash (OTC) data integrity and avoids costly returns resulting from unfulfilled modification requests.

g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound ord.title: Inbound Order Status Inquiry (ORDRSP / 869 / EDIFACT ODRSEL)
g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound ord.story: Computers need to talk to each other so people do not have to type the same thing twice. This process lets an external customer system ask SAP about the current state of a sales order, and SAP automatically replies with the answer using an electronic message. Without this, customers keep calling the desk to check if their stuff is moving. Technically, this manages the inbound EDI [Electronic Data Interchange] Order Status Inquiry message (X12 869 / EDIFACT ODRSEL) processing via ORDERS05 basic type, triggering a status check on the Sales Document and returning confirmation data.
g1|core|edi order to invoice|inbound ord.why_business_needs_it: Large B2B [Business-to-Business] customers automate order tracking to feed their own ERP [Enterprise Resource Planning] systems without human intervention. Implementing this integration reduces customer service overhead, eliminates manual inquiry processing delays, and provides 24/7 visibility into Order-to-Cash progression.

production_issues.verify: Create a test delivery with packing, trigger the DESADV output, and inspect segment E1EDL37 and E1EDL24 in transaction WE02.

g1|panel|edi order to invoice.otc_impact: EDI Order-to-Invoice automation is the operational backbone of high-volume Order-to-Cash, ensuring that customer purchase orders received electronically convert seamlessly into sales orders, deliveries, and billing documents without manual data entry. This digital handshake accelerates order processing times, eliminates transcription errors, and drastically reduces Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) by dispatching Advance Shipping Notices and invoices immediately upon goods issue. Any failure in this pipeline directly blocks sales creation, halts fulfillment, or delays customer payment, making robust interface monitoring and partner profile configurations mission-critical.

panel_qa.question: How do we handle incoming EDI orders with invalid materials or pricing discrepancies without stopping the entire inbound queue?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario involves high-volume customer orders arriving via EDI 850 that occasionally contain discontinued materials or unmapped customer-specific part numbers. SAP is configured using inbound IDoc error handling with workflow triggers and output processing codes via transaction WE42 to catch syntax or semantic failures in a suspense file. The key configuration involves setting up order reason codes, incompletion procedures, and customer material info records (VD01/MM01) alongside partner profiles in WE20 to route failed IDocs to transaction BD87. The leadership value is maintaining uninterrupted pipeline throughput, zero lost orders, and minimizing manual touch rates for order intake. Looking ahead, we utilize SAP Integration Suite to map incoming payloads dynamically against master data before staging. The weak answer is to say we just delete failed IDocs and ask the customer to resend them.
panel_qa.trap: We just delete failed IDocs and ask the customer to resend them.

panel_qa.question: What is our architecture for handling high-volume outbound invoicing (INVOIC/810) to ensure tax compliance and instant delivery to customer portals?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario requires generating and transmitting EDI 810 invoices immediately upon billing document creation in VF01/VF04. SAP is configured using the condition technique in output control (transaction NACE or BRF+ output management in S/4HANA) linked to message type RD00. The key configuration involves assigning medium 6 (EDI) to output determination procedures, linking partner functions (RE) in transaction WE20, and integrating with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance for electronic invoicing mandates. The leadership value is accelerating cash collection cycles, ensuring audit compliance, and eliminating paper-based postage costs. Looking ahead, we are standardizing on SAP S/4HANA output management via Business Rule Framework plus (BRF+). The weak answer is to assume standard print output works for EDI without configuring partner profiles.
panel_qa.trap: We assume standard print output works for EDI without configuring partner profiles.

panel_qa.question: How does automated inbound order change processing (ORDCHG/860) prevent fulfilling obsolete quantities or shipping to canceled locations?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario addresses customers modifying open sales orders via EDI 860 prior to outbound delivery creation. SAP is configured using ALE (Application Link Enabling) inbound function module IDOC_INPUT_ORDCHG mapped to sales document change types. The key configuration involves setting up change rules in Customizing under Sales and Distribution > Sales Documents > Sales Document Header > Define Sales Document Types for EDI, ensuring automatic rejection or update of schedule lines. The leadership value is mitigating shipping waste, avoiding costly returns, and maintaining high customer satisfaction through synchronized order books. Looking ahead, we monitor order change error logs daily via transaction WE02/WE05. The weak answer is stating that we manually check every inbound change against open orders.
panel_qa.trap: We state that we manually check every inbound change against open orders.

panel_qa.question: What working capital improvements do we achieve by automating the Outbound Advance Shipping Notice (DESADV/856)?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario involves sending precise pick and pack details to the customer the moment goods issue (VL02N) is posted. SAP is configured using output type DELV triggered from delivery processing, utilizing IDoc type DESADV01. The key configuration includes defining output determination for shipping, maintaining partner profiles in WE20 with message type DESADV, and activating handling unit management (HUM) if serial or pallet tracking is required. The leadership value is enabling customer automated goods receipt (AGR), speeding up invoice matching, and directly lowering Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) by days. Looking ahead, we leverage S/4HANA embedded Advanced Shipping and Receiving for seamless carrier integration. The weak answer is claiming ASNs are purely operational and have no impact on finance or cash flow.
panel_qa.trap: Claiming ASNs are purely operational and have no impact on finance or cash flow.

panel_qa.question: How do we govern master data synchronization between customer ERP systems and our SAP OTC environment to avoid EDI mapping failures?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: The business scenario prevents systematic EDI rejections caused by mismatched customer material numbers, unmapped units of measure, or expired partner GLN numbers. SAP is configured using customer material info records, customer specific condition records, and global location number (GLN) assignments in customer master records (XD01/BP). The key configuration involves maintaining segment filters and cross-reference tables in transaction V-08 and WE30 for IDoc extension management. The leadership value is achieving high first-pass order conversion rates and reducing operational overhead spent on exception handling. Looking ahead, we use Master Data Governance (MDG) to propagate partner updates cleanly. The weak answer is that master data discrepancies are handled ad-hoc by the customer service team via phone calls.
panel_qa.trap: Master data discrepancies are handled ad-hoc by the customer service team via phone calls.

doc_flow.what: Inbound customer purchase order creates the baseline sales document in SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash.
Sales order output determination triggers the outbound EDI order confirmation (ORDRSP) to communicate order acceptance back to the customer.
Intermediate Document for message type ORDRSP05 is generated, packaged, and transmitted to the partner network via defined ports.
Fulfillment processing initiates outbound delivery creation based on confirmed sales order quantities.
Customer invoice is generated from the delivery to finalize the order-to-cash revenue recognition cycle.
